newsitem.title: BRAZIL: AGF Brazil unit 1996 net profit lower.
newsitem.headline: AGF Brazil unit 1996 net profit lower.

text.p: Assurances Generales de France (AGF) Brazilian unit said its 1996 net profit fell 18.5 percent to 16.4 million reais ($15.6 milliion) when compared to 1995 earnings of 20.2 million reais.

AGF Brasil Seguros said in a statement that earnings dropped because premiums in 1996 grew only one percent as a result of strong competition which forced prices to fall despite an increase in the number of businesses.
It said insurance prices fell mostly in the auto sector due to increasing competition, restrictions to accept higher risks and new insurance products covering various types of risks at a lower price.
Earnings per 1,000 shares totalled 63.75 reais last year with premiums totalling 356.6 million reais, an increase of 52.1 percent over 1995 premiums of 234.5 million reais, it said.
Insurance claims rose 63 percent to 223.1 million reais in 1996 while the firm's net worth rose 9.5 percent to 142.1 million reais.
